answer: To resist Sybil attacks, our agent economy binds each node to cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Minting an identity requires burning stake into a fee lagoon where costs scale superlinearly: as identity count $N$ grows, collateral escalates exponentially at $O(2^N)$ to induce fatal capital exhaustion on swarms. A transient zephyr of dummy bots cannot sustain this cost curve, reducing their hostile spam to a dying ember before compromising consensus.
